title: Row Count Rumble
subtitle: The manager wants specific columns. Lazy querying won't cut it.
conceptSummary: SELECT column1, column2 picks ONLY the columns you need — like choosing which info to show.

dialogue.text: The manager at Pizza Palace wants a simple report. Just the order ID, date, and total price.
SELECT * would give them 8 columns. Way too much noise. We need to SELECT only the columns they care about.
Got it. I'll pick exactly the columns they need.

teachMoment.title: Picking Specific Columns
teachMoment.body:
Instead of *, you can name the exact columns:

SELECT order_id, order_date, total_price FROM orders

This is like reading only the Name and Grade columns from a report card — ignoring everything else.

task.instruction: Use the Query Builder blocks to SELECT only order_id, order_date, and total_price from the orders table.
task.startingQuery: SELECT order_id, order_date, total_price FROM orders
task.solution: SELECT order_id, order_date, total_price FROM orders

hints.text: Drag the SELECT block first, then pick only the 3 columns the manager asked for.
Full: SELECT order_id, order_date, total_price FROM orders

winDialogue.text: That's the report I wanted. Clean. Concise. Finally.
And I noticed something — order 1001 and 1003 both have the SHADOW42 code. Both from the same customer!

storyBeat: The mystery deepens: SHADOW42 keeps appearing on orders from Priya Sharma (customer ID 1). Is she the villain... or a victim?
